questions.q: State the empirical relationship between mean, median, and mode.
questions.a: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean. A wrong answer (e.g., "Mean = 3 Mode − 2 Median") shows the student has the formula backwards. The correct form has Mode on the left.

questions.q: For a moderately skewed distribution, if Mean = 18 and Median = 24, find the Mode.
questions.a: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean = 3(24) − 2(18) = 72 − 36 = 36. A wrong answer (e.g., Mode = 24 − 18 = 6) shows the student does not know the formula or is subtracting instead of applying the empirical relationship.

questions.q: If Mode = 30 and Mean = 20, find the Median using the empirical formula.
questions.a: From Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean: 30 = 3 Median − 2(20) = 3 Median − 40. So 3 Median = 70, Median = 70/3 ≈ 23.33. A wrong answer (e.g., Median = (30 + 20)/2 = 25) shows the student is averaging instead of using the formula.

questions.q: In a symmetric distribution, what is the relationship between mean, median, and mode?
questions.a: In a symmetric distribution, Mean = Median = Mode. The empirical formula Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean gives Mode = 3x − 2x = x, confirming all three are equal. A wrong answer (e.g., "they are different even in symmetric distributions") shows the student does not understand symmetry.

The formula is called empirical because it is based on observed patterns in real data, not derived from a mathematical theorem. It is an approximation that works well for moderately skewed, unimodal distributions but does not hold exactly for all distributions. A wrong answer (e.g., "because it was proved by an empiricist") shows a misunderstanding of the term "empirical" in statistics.

questions.q: A frequency distribution has Mean = 25, Median = 26, and Mode = 28. Verify whether the empirical relationship holds.
questions.a: Check: 3 × Median − 2 × Mean = 3(26) − 2(25) = 78 − 50 = 28. This equals the given Mode (28). So the empirical relationship holds. A wrong answer (e.g., "28 ≠ 26, so it doesn't hold") shows the student is comparing mode to median directly instead of checking the formula.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The empirical ______ between mean, median, and mode for a moderately skewed (asymmetric) frequency distribution is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.
Fill in the blank: In a perfectly symmetric ______ (like a bell curve), the mean, median, and mode all coincide at the same point.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can state the empirical formula Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean, explain when it is applicable (moderately skewed, unimodal distributions), use it to find any one of the three measures given the other two, and recognise when the formula does not apply (symmetric or bimodal distributions).
